Chapter 9: Maintaining Order Through Life’s Changes
Outer order isn’t something you achieve once and then forget about—it’s actually a living process that moves right along with the ups and downs of life. Think about those big moments—maybe you’re moving, starting a new job, welcoming a new family member, or dealing with a loss. Even the best systems can get shaken up during these times. And honestly, it’s completely normal for things to slip out of place, or for your daily routines to get turned upside down.
So, instead of chasing perfect control, what if you could approach these changes with a bit more flexibility—and a lot more self-compassion? Different stages of life really do call for different ways of organizing. Something that worked brilliantly before, might need a total re-think now.
Here are a few gentle strategies to help keep some order during life’s transitions:
First, prioritize the essentials. Try focusing your energy on the most important spots in your home—like the kitchen, your bedroom, or your workspace. It’s okay if the less-used areas aren’t perfect for a while.
Next, simplify your routines. When things get busy or stressful, pare back to just the basics you really need to function. There’s no need to stick to every detail if it’s just too much right now.
And maybe most importantly, allow for some temporary disorder. A little mess is just part of going through changes. Trust that you’ll find your way back to order when things settle down.
For example, imagine a new parent. Suddenly, those old cleaning routines don’t seem possible anymore. But by sticking to just a couple simple habits—like clearing out the sink at night, or keeping a basket handy for baby supplies—it’s still possible to carve out a bit of calm, even in the middle of chaos.
Transitions can also give you a chance to rethink what you truly need and value. Moving to a new home is a perfect time to let go of things that no longer serve you.
Most of all, be gentle with yourself—and with those around you—during times of change. Remember, outer order is meant to support your well-being, not measure your worth. By adapting your systems to fit whatever life brings, you can keep that sense of stability and comfort, even when everything else feels uncertain.
